findings.quote: During the season of that sacrifice, the law requires that these Salii not change their location for thirty days, wherever they may happen to be caught.
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna (`*` / `**`) between 'τοῖς θεοῖς:' and 'τριακονθήμερον μὴ μεταβαίνειν κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τῆς θυσίας, ἐν ᾗ ποτ᾽ ἂν χώρᾳ καταληφθῶσιν [οἱ σάλιοι οὗτοι]'. The sentence begins mid-clause; 'the law requires' is not in the Greek and 'these Salii' is an editorial bracket. The English reads as if whole.
findings.proposed_fix: [Text lost] ... not to move for thirty days at the time of the sacrifice, in whatever place they may be caught [these Salii].

units.note: Lacuna between the sacrifices sentence and the thirty-day rule.

findings.quote: the Romans took possession of Sardis and its citadel, and then Musaeus came from Antiochus under flag of truce.
findings.problem: Greek: 'τὰς Σάρδεις καὶ τὰς ἀκροπόλεις ἄρτι *** ἧκε Μουσαῖος' - a lacuna stands after ἄρτι and the verb of the first clause is missing; English joins the two clauses seamlessly. Also ἀκροπόλεις is plural.
findings.proposed_fix: the Romans took possession of Sardis and the citadels, just then [text lost] ... and Musaeus came from Antiochus to negotiate.

findings.quote: Publius said that the Romans never became harsher after victory.
findings.problem: Greek 'οὔτε νικήσαντας ἔφη Ῥωμαίους οὐδέποτε γενέσθαι βαρυτέρους, *' ends in a lacuna (continued by '** διὸ'); the οὔτε has no matching clause, so the sentence is incomplete and probably corrupt. English presents it as complete.
findings.proposed_fix: Publius said that the Romans, when victorious, never became harsher [text lost] ...

findings.quote: So they separated on those terms, and in the following days the Romans divided their forces.
findings.problem: Greek 'ταῖς δ᾽ ἑξῆς ἡμέραις οἱ Ῥωμαῖοι διεῖλον τὰς δυνάμεις * ** μετὰ δέ τινας ἡμέρας παραγενομένων τῶν ὁμήρων' has a lacuna after διεῖλον τὰς δυνάμεις; English runs straight on to the arrival of the hostages.
findings.proposed_fix: So they separated on those terms, and in the following days the Romans divided their forces [text lost] ...

units.note: Numbers checked: 15,000 Euboic talents = 500 + 2,500 + 12x1,000; 400 talents to Eumenes; 20 hostages; all correct.

findings.quote: but would continue entirely to leave those matters in Roman hands.
findings.problem: Greek 'ἀλλὰ μεῖναι *** τελέως διδοὺς ἐκείνοις τὴν ἐξουσίαν' has a lacuna after μεῖναι; the English supplies a smooth 'would continue ... to leave'.
findings.proposed_fix: but ... [text lost] ... entirely giving them the authority.

findings.quote: I would never knowingly give way to any living man.
findings.problem: Greek 'οὐδέποτ᾽ ἂν οὐδενὶ τῶν ὄντων ἐκχωρήσαιμι κατὰ δύναμιν': κατὰ δύναμιν = 'so far as lies in my power', not 'knowingly'.
findings.proposed_fix: I would never give way to anyone in the world, so far as lies in my power.

findings.quote: being the first in Asia and Greece to share your friendship and alliance
findings.problem: Greek 'πρῶτος μετασχὼν τῆς ὑμετέρας φιλίας καὶ συμμαχίας, σχεδὸν πάντων τῶν [κατὰ] τὴν Ἀσίαν καὶ τὴν Ἑλλάδα νεμομένων': σχεδὸν ('almost') is dropped; he was first of almost all those dwelling in Asia and Greece.
findings.proposed_fix: being the first of almost all who live in Asia and Greece to share your friendship and alliance
